Name: PostgreSQL
SDKs & notable repos: libpq, psycopg, pgx, JDBC; extensions via the contrib tree
Downloadable / offline docs: Full manual as PDF and HTML tarball per version: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/manuals/
Notes: The documentation is the benchmark the rest of the industry is measured against. The internals chapters and the source README files are real architecture documentation.

Name: PostgreSQL Wiki
SDKs & notable repos: Developer FAQ, todo lists, performance guidance
Notes: The Developer FAQ is the entry point for reading the source.

Name: MySQL
Downloadable / offline docs: Reference Manual downloadable as PDF, EPUB and HTML per version
Notes: Site 403s to bots; fine in a browser. The InnoDB chapters are the valuable part.

Name: MariaDB
SDKs & notable repos: Multiple storage engines: InnoDB, Aria, ColumnStore, MyRocks
Notes: The MySQL fork with the more open governance. Storage-engine variety makes it instructive.

Name: SQLite
SDKs & notable repos: Amalgamation build — the entire database as one C file
Downloadable / offline docs: Complete docs downloadable as a single archive; source amalgamation too
Notes: The most deployed database in the world and among the most readable. See `arch.html` for the architecture overview and `whyc.html` for the design rationale.

Name: SQLite architecture
SDKs & notable repos: VDBE, pager, B-tree — each layer documented separately
Notes: Read `arch.html` before the source. It saves days.

Name: CockroachDB
Notes: The `docs/RFCS/` directory in the repo is an exceptional record of distributed-SQL design decisions.

Name: YugabyteDB
SDKs & notable repos: PostgreSQL-compatible SQL layer over a distributed store; Cassandra-compatible API too
Notes: Reuses the actual PostgreSQL query layer — interesting as an architectural choice.

Name: TiDB
SDKs & notable repos: MySQL-compatible; TiKV storage layer is a separate readable project
Downloadable / offline docs: Docs site; PingCAP publishes extensive design blogs
Notes: PingCAP's engineering writing, and `awesome-database-learning`, are among the best free distributed-database education.

Name: Oracle Database
Downloadable / offline docs: Full documentation library downloadable per release
Notes: The Concepts guide is genuinely good and free; worth reading regardless of what you run.

Name: Microsoft SQL Server
SDKs & notable repos: Drivers for most languages; T-SQL reference
Notes: Documentation is open-source on GitHub — you can file issues against it.

Name: Google Cloud Spanner
SDKs & notable repos: Client libraries in all major languages
Downloadable / offline docs: Docs site; the Spanner papers are free PDFs
Notes: Read the 2012 OSDI paper and the 2017 SIGMOD paper together — external consistency via TrueTime is the central idea.

Name: IBM Db2
Notes: IBM Docs 403s to automated clients; loads normally in a browser.

Name: DuckDB
SDKs & notable repos: In-process analytics; Python, R, C++, WASM, CLI
Notes: The SQLite of analytics. Also an unusually readable modern vectorized engine.

Name: ClickHouse
SDKs & notable repos: HTTP and native protocols; clients everywhere
Notes: Extremely fast columnar OLAP. The source is a good study of vectorized execution and compression.

Name: Apache Druid
SDKs & notable repos: Real-time analytics with sub-second queries over streams

Name: Snowflake
Notes: The 2016 SIGMOD paper on the architecture is the best explanation of storage/compute separation.

Name: Google BigQuery
Notes: Dremel's descendant; the Dremel paper is still the key reading.

Name: Amazon Redshift
Downloadable / offline docs: AWS docs downloadable as PDF per guide

Name: RocksDB
SDKs & notable repos: C++, Java, Rust, Go bindings; used inside dozens of other databases
Downloadable / offline docs: Wiki is the real documentation and it is extensive
Notes: The LSM-tree implementation most systems build on. The wiki's tuning guide is a distributed-systems education in itself.

Name: LevelDB
SDKs & notable repos: The original compact LSM store from Google
Notes: Small enough to read completely. Read before RocksDB.

Name: LMDB
SDKs & notable repos: Memory-mapped B+tree with MVCC, single writer
Notes: The counterpoint to LSM trees. ~10k lines, copy-on-write B+tree.

Name: WiredTiger
SDKs & notable repos: MongoDB's storage engine; both B-tree and LSM modes

Name: Apache Arrow
SDKs & notable repos: In-memory columnar standard; implementations in 12+ languages
Notes: The columnar format spec is short and worth reading directly — it underpins most modern analytics.

Name: Apache Parquet
SDKs & notable repos: The on-disk columnar format; encodings and statistics documented in the spec
Notes: Read the encoding section — dictionary and RLE encoding explain most of the compression wins.

Name: Apache ORC
SDKs & notable repos: Columnar format from the Hive lineage

Name: Apache Iceberg
SDKs & notable repos: Java, Python, Rust, Go implementations; REST catalog spec
Downloadable / offline docs: Table spec is a single readable document
Notes: Currently the de facto open table format. Read the spec — snapshot isolation over object storage is the whole trick.

Name: Delta Lake
Notes: The transaction log protocol is the thing to read.

Name: Use The Index, Luke
SDKs & notable repos: SQL indexing explained for developers, across five database engines
Notes: The single most useful practical resource on indexing. Most query performance problems end here.

Name: Modern SQL
SDKs & notable repos: What SQL has gained since 1992 — window functions, CTEs, JSON, MATCH_RECOGNIZE
Notes: Same author as Use The Index, Luke. Corrects the assumption that SQL stopped evolving.

Name: PostgreSQL Exercises
SDKs & notable repos: Graded SQL exercises against a real schema

Name: DB-Engines Ranking
Notes: Methodology is popularity-based, not technical. Useful for trends, not for selection.

Category: 7. Query engines, streaming and the surrounding ecosystem
Name: Apache DataFusion
SDKs & notable repos: Extensible query engine in Rust built on Arrow; used as a component inside other databases
Notes: The easiest modern query engine to read and embed. Good entry point to vectorized execution in Rust.

Category: 7. Query engines, streaming and the surrounding ecosystem
Name: Apache Calcite
SDKs & notable repos: SQL parser, planner and cost-based optimizer as a reusable library
Notes: Used by Flink, Druid, Hive and others. The rule-based optimizer is the part worth studying.

Category: 7. Query engines, streaming and the surrounding ecosystem
Name: Trino
SDKs & notable repos: Distributed SQL over many data sources; connector SPI
Notes: The Presto fork that most of the community moved to. The connector architecture is well documented.

Category: 7. Query engines, streaming and the surrounding ecosystem
Name: Polars
SDKs & notable repos: Arrow-backed DataFrame library in Rust with Python bindings; lazy query optimization
Notes: Shows query-optimizer ideas applied to DataFrames. Faster than pandas and architecturally more interesting.

Category: 7. Query engines, streaming and the surrounding ecosystem
Name: Materialize
SDKs & notable repos: Incremental view maintenance over streams, built on timely/differential dataflow
Notes: Differential dataflow is one of the genuinely novel ideas in this space. Worth reading even if you never deploy it.

Category: 7. Query engines, streaming and the surrounding ecosystem
Name: RisingWave
SDKs & notable repos: Streaming database with PostgreSQL wire compatibility

Category: 7. Query engines, streaming and the surrounding ecosystem
Name: Debezium
SDKs & notable repos: Change data capture from databases into Kafka
Notes: The connector internals teach you a lot about how replication logs actually work in each database.

Category: 7. Query engines, streaming and the surrounding ecosystem
Name: Vitess
SDKs & notable repos: Horizontal sharding middleware for MySQL, built at YouTube
Notes: The reference implementation of sharding a single-node database without rewriting it.

Category: 7. Query engines, streaming and the surrounding ecosystem
Name: pgvector
SDKs & notable repos: Vector similarity search as a PostgreSQL extension
Notes: Readable C, and a good example of how PostgreSQL’s extension and index APIs work.

Category: 7. Query engines, streaming and the surrounding ecosystem
Name: SQLGlot
SDKs & notable repos: SQL parser, transpiler and optimizer in pure Python across 20+ dialects
Notes: A readable SQL parser and optimizer you can actually step through in a debugger.

Name: arXiv
SDKs & notable repos: Preprints across all of CS; most systems, ML and PL work appears here before publication
Downloadable / offline docs: Every paper is a free PDF. Bulk access documented at https://info.arxiv.org/help/bulk_data/index.html; a full-text API at export.arxiv.org
Notes: Not peer-reviewed. Treat an arXiv-only paper as a claim, not a result — but it is where you will read almost everything first.

Name: ar5iv
SDKs & notable repos: Renders any arXiv paper as responsive HTML instead of PDF
Notes: Makes papers readable on a phone and searchable in-page. Underused.

Name: alphaXiv
SDKs & notable repos: arXiv papers with a public comment and discussion layer
Notes: Useful when a paper is contested — the discussion often contains the critique you were looking for.

Name: Semantic Scholar
SDKs & notable repos: 200M+ papers with citation graph, influential-citation scoring and TLDR summaries
Downloadable / offline docs: Free Graph API (https://www.semanticscholar.org/product/api), bulk datasets available on request
Notes: The best free citation graph. 'Highly influential citations' is a genuinely useful filter for finding what actually mattered.

Name: OpenAlex
SDKs & notable repos: Fully open catalogue of works, authors, venues and institutions; successor to Microsoft Academic Graph
Downloadable / offline docs: Entirely free API with no key required; complete database snapshots downloadable
Notes: The only large-scale bibliographic database that is open all the way down, including bulk snapshots.

Name: DBLP
SDKs & notable repos: Authoritative CS bibliography — complete author and venue listings
Notes: The fastest way to find everything a given researcher has published, and to see a conference's full programme by year.

Name: OpenReview
SDKs & notable repos: ICLR, NeurIPS, COLM and dozens of other venues — papers plus the full review threads
Notes: Reading the reviews and author rebuttals teaches you how the field evaluates work. Nothing else exposes this.

Name: CORE
SDKs & notable repos: Aggregates 300M+ open-access papers from repositories worldwide
Notes: Good for finding the green open-access copy when a publisher's version is paywalled.

Name: Unpaywall
SDKs & notable repos: Finds legal free copies of paywalled papers via DOI
Notes: Legal, author-deposited copies only. Install the extension and most paywalls simply stop appearing.

Name: Papers We Love
SDKs & notable repos: A curated, categorised repository of classic CS papers with local meetup talks
Downloadable / offline docs: Repo cloneable; many PDFs mirrored in-repo
Notes: The best starting point if you do not yet know which papers matter in a subfield.

Name: The Morning Paper (archive)
Notes: No longer updated, but the back catalogue of ~1000 summarised papers is one of the great free CS resources.

Name: USENIX Proceedings
SDKs & notable repos: OSDI, SOSP (co-published), NSDI, ATC, FAST, Security — the core systems venues
Downloadable / offline docs: Every paper free, immediately, with no membership. Often with recorded talks
Notes: USENIX made everything open access years before the rest of the field. If a systems paper exists, check here first.

Name: ACM Digital Library
SDKs & notable repos: SIGMOD, ASPLOS, PLDI, POPL, SoCC and the ACM journals
Downloadable / offline docs: Partly open: ACM Open and author-paid OA papers are free; others are paywalled
Notes: 403s to automated clients; loads in a browser. For paywalled items, check arXiv, the author's homepage or Unpaywall first — the free copy usually exists.

Name: IEEE Xplore
SDKs & notable repos: ISCA, MICRO, HPCA and the IEEE journals
Notes: Almost always worth searching the author's page or arXiv instead. Architecture authors in particular post preprints widely.

Name: DROPS / LIPIcs (Dagstuhl)
SDKs & notable repos: ECOOP, ITP, CONCUR, SAT and many theory venues
Downloadable / offline docs: 100% open access, free PDFs, Creative Commons licensed
Notes: A fully open publisher. Every paper, always free, no exceptions.

Name: arXiv cs.DB (Databases)
Notes: Most PVLDB submissions appear here first.

Name: PVLDB
SDKs & notable repos: Proceedings of the VLDB Endowment — the main database venue
Downloadable / offline docs: 100% open access, every volume, free PDFs
Notes: Fully open since inception. The single best free database paper archive.

Name: CIDR
SDKs & notable repos: Conference on Innovative Data Systems Research — biennial, visionary, short papers
Notes: Often the most interesting reading of the three main venues. Industry systems get described here first.

Name: ACM SIGMOD
Downloadable / offline docs: Proceedings via ACM DL; many authors post preprints
Notes: Check arXiv or the author's page before hitting the ACM paywall.

Name: Database of Databases (dbdb.io)
SDKs & notable repos: A catalogue of 1000+ database systems with their architectural properties and references
Notes: CMU-maintained. Filter by storage model, concurrency control or query interface to find comparable systems fast.

Name: The Red Book
SDKs & notable repos: Readings in Database Systems, 5th edition — classic papers with editorial commentary
Notes: Stonebraker and Hellerstein telling you why each paper mattered. Read the commentary even if you skip the papers.

Name: CMU 15-445 Database Systems
Notes: Andy Pavlo's undergraduate course. Full video lectures, slides, and C++ projects where you build a buffer pool, B+tree, query executor and concurrency control. Free and complete — better than most paid programmes.

Name: CMU Database Group YouTube
Notes: Every lecture, plus the seminar series where real system architects explain their designs.

Name: db.cs.cmu.edu
Notes: The group's hub: courses, seminars, the Database of Databases.

Name: Berkeley CS186
Notes: The other strong public undergraduate course. Different emphasis, good second pass.

Name: Use The Index, Luke
Notes: Learn indexing properly before learning anything else about performance.

Name: Modern SQL
Notes: Window functions and CTEs will change how you write queries.

Name: PostgreSQL Exercises
Notes: Practise against a real schema with immediate feedback.

Name: SQL Style Guide
Notes: Short. Adopt it and stop arguing about formatting.

Name: SQLite architecture overview
Notes: Short, precise, and describes a complete database. The best first look inside one.

Name: Why SQLite is written in C
Notes: Engineering rationale stated plainly. Instructive about trade-offs.

Name: SQLite source
Notes: Approachable, heavily commented, heavily tested.

Name: DuckDB docs
Notes: Install in one line and have a modern vectorized engine on your laptop.

Name: PostgreSQL manual
SDKs & notable repos: The reference documentation to learn to navigate
Notes: The gold standard. Learn its structure; you will return for years.

Name: MySQL reference manual
SDKs & notable repos: The reference documentation to learn to navigate
Notes: Specifically the InnoDB chapters.

Name: SQLite documentation
SDKs & notable repos: The reference documentation to learn to navigate
Notes: Unusually complete for a project of its size.

Name: databass.dev
Notes: Companion site to Database Internals — storage engines and distributed systems, clearly explained.

Name: Designing Data-Intensive Applications
Notes: Kleppmann's book. The chapters on replication, partitioning and consistency are the standard shared reference.

Name: The Red Book (Readings in Database Systems)
Notes: Curated classic papers with editorial commentary. Free online, 5th edition.

Name: Papers We Love
Notes: Start here when you do not yet know which papers matter. Curated by subfield, with recorded talks.

Name: The Morning Paper archive
Notes: Around a thousand papers summarised in plain language. No longer updated; still one of the best free CS resources.

Name: Semantic Scholar
Notes: Free citation graph. The 'highly influential citations' filter is the fastest way to find what a paper actually changed.

Name: Unpaywall
Notes: Install the extension. Most paywalls stop appearing, legally, because the author deposited a copy.

Name: ar5iv
Notes: Read any arXiv paper as HTML instead of a two-column PDF. Swap arxiv.org/abs for ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html.

Name: CMU 15-721 Advanced Database Systems
Notes: In-memory, columnar, vectorized and compiled query execution. Paper-driven, all video online. The best advanced database course available free.

Name: CMU 15-445
Notes: Do the projects even if you only watch 15-721. The implementation work is where the learning is.

Name: CMU Database Group seminar series
Notes: Architects of real systems explaining their internals — Snowflake, DuckDB, TiDB and dozens more.

Name: Berkeley CS186
Notes: Public projects with a solid concurrency-control component.

Name: DuckDB source
Notes: Modern vectorized execution in readable C++. The best codebase to study push-based execution.

Name: ClickHouse source
Notes: Extreme-performance columnar execution; aggressive specialization everywhere.

Name: Apache Arrow columnar spec
Notes: Short spec that explains why everything in analytics converged on this layout.

Name: Parquet format spec
Notes: Encodings, statistics, predicate pushdown — all in one document.

Name: Apache Calcite
Notes: Cost-based optimization as a reusable component. Read the rule system.

Name: RocksDB wiki
Notes: LSM compaction strategies, write stalls, tuning. Deeper than most textbooks.

Name: RocksDB source
Notes: The reference LSM implementation.

Name: LevelDB
Notes: Read this first — same ideas, a fraction of the code.

Name: LMDB
Notes: Copy-on-write B+tree with MVCC. The intellectual opposite of LSM; study both.

Name: WiredTiger
Notes: B-tree and LSM in one engine, in production under MongoDB.

Name: databass.dev
Notes: Ties the storage-engine literature together coherently.

Name: CockroachDB RFCs
Notes: The `docs/RFCS/` directory records real distributed-SQL design arguments in detail. Rare and valuable.

Name: TiDB
Notes: Percolator-style transactions over a separate TiKV storage layer.

Name: awesome-database-learning
Notes: PingCAP's curated path through papers, courses and source. Excellent.

Name: YugabyteDB
Notes: Reuses PostgreSQL's query layer over a distributed store.

Name: Cloud Spanner docs
Notes: TrueTime and external consistency, documented by the people who shipped it.

Name: Designing Data-Intensive Applications
Notes: Chapter 7 and 9 on transactions and consistency remain the clearest treatment.

Name: Apache Iceberg spec
Notes: Read the spec, not the marketing. Snapshot isolation over object storage.

Name: Delta Lake protocol
Notes: The transaction log design, stated precisely.

Name: Apache Hudi
Notes: Copy-on-write versus merge-on-read trade-offs.

Name: Snowflake docs
Notes: Separation of storage and compute as realised commercially.

Name: The Red Book
Notes: Start here. Classic papers with commentary explaining why each mattered.

Name: VLDB / PVLDB
Notes: All papers free. The main database research venue.

Name: ACM SIGMOD
Notes: The other main venue. ACM DL 403s to bots; accessible in a browser, and most papers are also on authors' pages.

Name: CIDR
Notes: Biennial, visionary, short papers. Often the most interesting reading of the three.

Name: awesome-database-learning
Notes: Also a good paper index organised by subsystem.
